title: Bioelectric networks derive distinct morphologies from one genome

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Bioelectric networks derive distinct morphologies from one genome

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Physiological bioelectric networks are a previously unrecognized input by which distinct morphologies, including those of other species, can be derived from the same genome, as shown by gap-junction perturbation in G. dorotocephala.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.1. Perturbation of Bioelectric Networks Produces Inter-Species Morphological Change

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Here, we identify a novel physiological input into the process by which distinct morphologies can be derived from the same genome: physiological bioelectric networks.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “3. Discussion › 3.1. Perturbation of Bioelectric Networks Produces Inter-Species Morphological Change”. Scope: Planarian head regeneration (G. dorotocephala), proposed as a general input to morphogenesis

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-12: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The paper's experiment directly addresses same-genome morphological plasticity in a restricted case. It does not establish a general input mechanism across morphogenesis or separate electrical from biochemical gap-junction signaling.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Hold genotype constant, perturb bioelectric connectivity, and quantify reproducible shifts among anatomical outcomes while measuring voltage state. Existing Girardia observations test this in one regeneration context; broader confirmation requires additional systems.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The general claim extends beyond the sampled species and organ.

One pharmacological perturbation does not isolate bioelectric networks from other gap-junction cargo.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.75
data existence: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Same-genome, different-anatomy is testable by pairing sequence with shape. Public nucleotide records identify the species and do not include the treated cohort. The paper's wild-type premise and the morphological outcome are published summaries, not a dataset that can confirm the physiological input.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Hold genotype fixed by sequencing treated and control fragments, perturb gap-junction connectivity, and test whether head shape moves among the reference species forms. Shape change with an unchanged genome would support a physiological input; sequence differences tracking the new shapes, or no shape change, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Treated animals were not deposited as sequenced genotypes paired with head shape.

Octanol can alter shape through non-bioelectric toxicity, so shape change alone does not identify the network as the input.
